observed_mechanics: 0x00a98400 SUB ESP,0x38 -- the only frame instruction. It makes ESP 0x38 below the entry stack pointer and is what makes [ESP+0x40] at 0x00a98403 read entry_ESP+0x8.

0x00a98403 MOV EAX,[ESP+0x40] -- EAX = the word at entry_ESP+0x8, the SECOND ordinary stack argument. It is the first of two reads of the same displacement and the two name DIFFERENT arguments; see record_incompleteness.
0x00a98407 MOVSS XMM0,[EAX+0x4] -- the first of four dword loads out of argument 2.
0x00a9840c MOV DX,[EAX+0x2] -- a WORD load, not a dword: two bytes, and the high sixteen bits of DX keep whatever a 32-bit register write left there. It is stored as a word at 0x00a98444.
0x00a98410 MOVSS [ESP+0x4],XMM0 -- frame byte 0x04. Six bytes of encoding, not five: the ModRM byte 0x44 selects a SIB byte for an ESP-relative operand.
0x00a98416 / 0x00a9841b MOVSS XMM0,[EAX+0x8] then MOVSS [ESP+0x8],XMM0 -- frame bytes 0x08..0x0b.
0x00a98421 MOVSS XMM0,[EAX+0xc] -- the third of the four dword loads, and the value is stored eleven instructions later, at 0x00a9842c.
0x00a98426 PUSH ESI -- the frame's only save. It is also what makes the displacement of the next store land where it does: [ESP+0x10] at 0x00a9842c is frame byte 0x0c, not frame byte 0x10.

0x00a98427 MOV ESI,ECX -- the only read of ECX in the body (obs-0013) and the register the machine record names as the RECEIVER. It is a lifetime copy, not a reach: nothing is ever loaded or stored through ESI.
0x00a98429 MOV CX,[EAX] -- a WORD load of argument 2's first two bytes, and the body's only write to ECX (obs-0015). It happens after the copy into ESI, so the copy sees the entry value of ECX.

0x00a9842c MOVSS [ESP+0x10],XMM0 -- frame bytes 0x0c..0x0f, reached with one word pushed. The two bytes at frame 0x0c and 0x0d are therefore written by this store and NOT by the 0x00a9841b one, which wrote 0x08..0x0b.
0x00a98432 MOVSS XMM0,[EAX+0x10] -- the last load out of argument 2 in the body, and the last write to XMM0 anywhere in it. Its only consumer is the store at 0x00a98449.

0x00a98437 ADD EAX,0x14 -- the pushed base is argument 2 + 0x14, and this is the only arithmetic the body does on argument 2. The window the first callee is therefore given is argument 2 + 0x14 .. argument 2 + 0x37.
0x00a9843a MOV [ESP+0x4],CX -- frame bytes 0x00..0x01, reached with two words pushed.
0x00a9843f PUSH EAX -- the first callee's stack word, consumed by that callee's own RET 0x4.

0x00a98440 LEA ECX,[ESP+0x1c] -- the first callee's hidden receiver: with two words pushed, [ESP+0x1c] is frame byte 0x14, so the window is frame 0x14..0x37, exactly the rest of the 0x38-byte reservation.
0x00a98444 MOV [ESP+0xa],DX -- frame bytes 0x02..0x03, reached with two words pushed.
0x00a98449 MOVSS [ESP+0x18],XMM0 -- frame bytes 0x10..0x13, reached with two words pushed.

0x00a9844f CALL 0x0041cb40 -- direct, rel32, with one word pushed and consumed by the callee. The body's first and only unconditional call. That callee's own body was read: it copies nine dwords, 0x24 bytes, from its stack word to offsets 0x00..0x20 of its hidden receiver, and ends in RET 0x4.

0x00a98454 MOV EAX,[ESP+0x40] -- the SECOND read of the same displacement, and the one the linear ESP walk could not resolve. With the first callee's RET 0x4 accounted for, ESP is one word below the frame, so [ESP+0x40] is entry_ESP+0x4: argument 1, a different word from the one read at 0x00a98403.
0x00a98458 PUSH EAX -- argument 1, handed on unexamined.
0x00a98459 LEA ECX,[ESP+0x8] -- the second callee's hidden receiver, frame byte 0x00 with two words pushed. It is the same address the third callee is handed as its stack word.
0x00a9845d CALL 0x00537f40 -- direct, rel32, with one word pushed and consumed by the callee (RET 0x4 at 00537ff5).

0x00a98462 LEA ECX,[ESP+0x4] -- with one word pushed, [ESP+0x4] is frame byte 0x00 again. The LEA and the PUSH that follows it are how the ADDRESS of the frame head gets onto the stack, and they compute the same value the LEA at 0x00a98459 computed three instructions earlier.
0x00a98466 PUSH ECX -- the third callee's stack word.
0x00a98467 LEA ECX,[ESI+0x18] -- the ONLY use the body makes of the receiver: it forms receiver+0x18 and nothing ever reads or writes there.
0x00a9846a CALL 0x00537dc0 -- direct, rel32, with one word pushed and consumed by the callee (RET 0x4 at 00537e94). It is the last call, and its result in EAX is what reaches the caller unaltered.
0x00a9846f POP ESI -- restores ESI (obs-0027, REG_RESTORE), the only register the body saves.
0x00a98470 ADD ESP,0x38 -- gives back the reservation, landing exactly on the entry stack pointer, which is only true if all three pushes were consumed by their own callees.
0x00a98473 RET 0x8 -- pops the return address and drops two four-byte words: stack_cleanup_bytes 8, owner callee, confidence OBSERVED.
CONTROL FLOW. One basic block, thirty-one instructions, no conditional branch and no indirect transfer. There is no path on which the epilogue is not reached, and exactly one return site.

The body writes nothing through any pointer it did not push. Its only stores are the six frame stores and nothing else: there is no store through the receiver, and none through either argument. Argument 2 is read and read through; argument 1 is read, pushed and handed on, and never dereferenced.

The body performs no virtual dispatch: all three callees are immediate operands, matching the machine dispatch record's indirect_calls 0, vtable_shaped_loads 0 and call_offsets []. The body is itself a slot occupant -- 0x00a98400 is the word at 0x014587a0, slot 6 of the table based at 0x01458788 -- which is the opposite of dispatching: it never reads the word at the receiver's +0x00.

GLOBALS. None. The thirty-one instructions name no data-segment address; the immediates that are addresses are 0x0041cb40, 0x00537f40 and 0x00537dc0, all inside .text. The record's globals category is empty and the xref export carries no data-reference edge type for this VA.

xrefs. ghidra_function reports xref_count 1 with 0 CALLERS (dependencies.callers is empty with callers_truncated false, so that is a measured absence rather than a truncated one) and the single reference is the data word at 0x014587a0. The data-side association is what R1-VFT used to place the receiver in ECX. No class, slot identity or dispatch shape is inferred from it beyond the address and the slot index the record itself names.
CONVENTION. The machine record determines __thiscall (INFERRED, single candidate): R1-VFT from the vftable slot at 0x01458788 plus the body reading its incoming ECX, C6B from the callee-side cleanup.
semantic_findings: The body is a straight-line three-callee wrapper with no branch at all. 0x0041cb40, then 0x00537f40, then 0x00537dc0, on every execution, in that order, with nothing between them that can be skipped.

The twenty bytes at the head of the frame are a byte-for-byte copy of the first twenty bytes of the SECOND stack argument, reassembled from two word loads and four dword loads in ascending address order. That is a property of the listing and the model test checks it as one, against the argument's own bytes, over seven different argument patterns.

The two word loads are word loads. MOV DX,[EAX+0x2] and MOV CX,[EAX] each touch two bytes and each store two bytes, so argument 2's bytes 0x00..0x03 reach the frame as two separate 16-bit copies rather than one 32-bit one. A reconstruction that loaded or stored a dword there would be a different function, and the byte witness pins the 66-prefixed forms at 0x00a9840c, 0x00a98429, 0x00a9843a and 0x00a98444.

The receiver is present in ECX and is never dereferenced. Those are two separate facts and the second is the sharp one: the body copies the receiver, forms ONE address from it, hands that address to a callee, and not one of those operations inspects a byte. The machine record agrees (receiver present true, register ECX, bounds_only true, offsets [], written_through 0). The type is therefore an undefined struct -- no pointee, no field, no size -- even though the register carries a receiver. An earlier revision of a sibling package read the absence of a dereference as the absence of a receiver, which the machine record corrects: R1-VFT places the receiver from the vftable slot, not from a dereference.

The receiver's ONE use is an address, not a value, and 0x18 is a displacement rather than a field. Nothing in these 118 bytes reads or writes receiver+0x18, so the listing fixes the arithmetic and fixes nothing whatever about what lives there. No layout is claimed in either direction and the displacement is carried as an immediate out of 0x00a98467.

The FIRST stack argument is never looked through. It is loaded at 0x00a98454, pushed at 0x00a98458 and handed to 0x00537f40, and no instruction in the body dereferences it. The model test exploits that and drives it over values that are not mapped at all, which is only sound BECAUSE the body never looks: a reconstruction that read through it would fault, and this is the cheapest available refutation of one.

The SECOND stack argument is read at six displacements and then had 0x14 added to it and pushed. So the body reaches argument 2 + 0x00, +0x02, +0x04, +0x08, +0x0c, +0x10 and, through the first callee, +0x14 .. +0x37. That is 0x38 bytes of it in total, which is the same size as the frame; the coincidence is arithmetic, not a claim that the two are related.

Cleanup is symmetric on the way IN and asymmetric in the making. All three callees are callee-popped with a four-byte immediate, which is what lets the body leave the stack exactly as it found it, and the OUTER RET 0x8 then drops the two words its caller pushed. Three callee-popped pushes, one callee-popped return: the whole body is callee-cleaned, which is the shape C6B combines with the ECX receiver to name __thiscall.

No virtual dispatch is performed by the body, and no class is claimed. The record does place this VA at slot 6 of the table at 0x01458788, and that association is the EVIDENCE for the receiver (receiver_provenance vftable_slot_dispatch), not a claim that the body dispatches: the body contains no indirect transfer at all, and it is a slot occupant rather than a dispatcher. A slot is not a class, and this binary carries no MSVC RTTI.

The return is void on the listing's own evidence and that is a reading rather than a recovered fact. The machine record's RT1 rule names XMM0 at APPROXIMATION on the basis that an SSE instruction appears in the body, which is not a statement about a return; this package records that claim and does not adopt it, and the divergence is carried in unresolved_questions rather than resolved in either direction.
unresolved_questions: THE MACHINE RECORD'S STACK-ARGUMENT LIST IS INCOMPLETE, AND THIS PACKAGE COMPLETES IT RATHER THAN COPYING IT. abi_derived.stack_arguments enumerates one slot (entry_ESP+0x8, ordinal 2) with gaps 1 and abstains with "flow_not_modelled: the linear ESP walk ends at +12, so the listing is not one path". This package reads two stack arguments, at entry_ESP+0x4 and entry_ESP+0x8, on the evidence of the three callees' own RET 0x4 terminators and of the frame arithmetic closing at exactly the entry stack pointer. The reading is stated with its evidence in observed_original_abi.record_incompleteness and the record itself is left unedited. A reviewer who rejects the reading would have to also reject that those three functions end in RET 0x4, which is a fact about the image rather than about this body.

THE RETURN REGISTER. The machine record names XMM0 at confidence APPROXIMATION under rule RT1, whose stated basis is "an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body". The listing contains no instruction that places a value in a return register at the terminator, so this package declares void and records the machine's claim without adopting it. Nothing here settles what a caller of this body does read, and no return type beyond the source-side choice is claimed.

THE RECEIVER'S IDENTITY. __thiscall says the receiver arrives in ECX; it does not say what the receiver IS. The body never dereferences it and never adjusts it, and the only code reference to this address is a word in a table rather than a this-adjusting stub, so no base relationship is observable from here at all. No class, no vtable identity, no receiver type, no object size, no vtable-pointer offset and no field are claimed, and none is guessed.

WHETHER THE RECEIVER IS A POINTER AT ALL. It is a 32-bit word that is copied, added to and handed to a callee. Nothing in these 118 bytes inspects the value, so nothing here can say whether it addresses an object. The type is left undefined (struct Receiver;) and no pointee is named.
WHAT LIES AT RECEIVER+0x18. The body forms the address and hands it over; it never reads or writes there. The displacement is certain and the contents are not in evidence at all.

THE CLASS THAT OWNS THE TABLE 0x01458788, AND WHETHER IT IS A vptr-BACKED VTABLE AT ALL. R1-VFT calls the table it reasons about a sound vptr-backed vftable, and GhidraMCP /read_memory at 0x01458770 for 48 bytes shows seven consecutive .text words of which this body is the seventh, but this binary carries no MSVC RTTI and no SDK name is recorded for the table. The receiver determination does not need a class and none is claimed. The other six words are transcribed in the staging header as bytes at an address, and nothing is inferred from them beyond their being code addresses.

WHAT 0x0041cb40, 0x00537f40 AND 0x00537dc0 ARE. None is named in the image, none is owned by a package, and this package gives none of them a semantic name. For 0x0041cb40 its own body was read (64 instructions) and it copies 0x24 bytes from its stack argument to its hidden receiver; that copy is modelled and nothing else about it is claimed. For the other two only the call shape is claimed: a hidden receiver in ECX and one callee-popped four-byte word.

THE MEANING OF THE TWENTY FRAME BYTES AT S+0x00 AND OF THE 0x24 BYTES AT S+0x14. Both are located, sized and, for the first, traced to their sources in argument 2. What they MEAN -- two 16-bit quantities and four single-precision values, or something else -- is not in evidence and is not claimed. The machine test checks them as bytes against the argument's own bytes and asserts no interpretation.

THE MEANING OF ARGUMENT 1. It is read, pushed and handed on, and never dereferenced, so nothing in these 118 bytes constrains what it is. It is declared Word* because that is the width of the slot it occupies, not because anything here shows it points at a struct. The model test drives it over eight values, including unmapped ones, precisely because its value does not matter.

DECOMPILATION UNAVAILABLE. Both the persisted record and the live bridge report none (the evidence pack's decompilation category reports availability missing and no persisted or live decompilation for this target). Every claim here is from the disassembly listing, the ABI envelope, and bytes and terminators read back out of the image.

The source span now carries the token and observed_original_abi.calling_convention now states __thiscall. The RETURN SEMANTICS arm reads the canonical return_type claim and the source span's declared return type, which agree at void. mutation_evidence.byte_witness_layers: The test carries TWO independent byte witnesses, and the SM mutations were run against both. The first is kTargetBytes in the header, which is the binary's own /read_memory transcript. The second is the set of hard-coded literals inside case W (W9 through W26), each written as an opcode prefix in the test file itself and not read from the header. SM1 through SM4 are consistent with the FIRST and are all killed by the SECOND, which is why they do not survive even before behaviour is consulted. Their purpose was to show that the two are genuinely separate; the run showed something slightly different and more useful, which is that the header transcript alone is not the only byte authority in the file.
mutation_evidence.behaviour_only_remeasurement: A second pass rebuilt each of the four SM mutants with EVERY check in case_the_entry_emits_the_target_bytes replaced by a macro that discards its condition, leaving only the executed cases. All four still died: SM1 at A13, SM2 at A13, SM3 at M2, SM4 at A13. So the behavioural layer is an independent witness and not a restatement of the bytes.
mutation_evidence.note: The SM mutations are the ones that matter. M1, M2, M5 through M10 and M20 change the emitted bytes without the transcript and are killed by the byte comparison alone, which is the point of pinning the reconstruction to the binary's own /read_memory output rather than to a second assembly of the same instructions. The SM mutations change the emitted bytes AND the transcript together, so the first witness is silent; they are killed by the second byte witness, and by executed behaviour when even that is removed. M11 through M19 change carried data and are killed by literal comparisons and by static_asserts, which is what makes carrying the determination as data worth anything: changing the data is what must be caught, and it is.

The convention this package declares is the machine's, transcribed field for field from evidence pack category abi_derived, and it is carried in the staging header as data rather than only in prose so that a later edit that reverts it fails the model test instead of passing quietly.

THE STACK-ARGUMENT READING IS THE ONE PLACE WHERE THIS PACKAGE GOES BEYOND THE MACHINE RECORD, and it is flagged as such in three separate fields rather than quietly adopted. The record abstains from a complete stack walk and enumerates one slot; this package reads two, with the three callees' own RET 0x4 terminators and the closing frame arithmetic as its evidence. Nothing was edited in the record to make the two agree.

One harness bug was found and fixed in this package's own model test during the run, and it is worth recording because it is a trap rather than a typo. The first revision derived the body's frame base from the stack pointer sampled AFTER the call returns, subtracting the RET immediate. That is wrong by one word, because `ret imm16` pops the return address FIRST and only then adds its immediate, so a post-call sample sits FOUR bytes above entry_ESP + kRetImmediateBytes and not on it. The symptom was that every frame-relative address the observers reported came back four bytes below what the listing computes, while the stack-balance checks -- which are pure deltas and never touch an absolute value -- all passed, so nothing looked broken except the two checks that happened to compare an absolute address. The harness now samples the stack pointer immediately before the CALL, where the callee's entry ESP is exactly one word below it, and carries that word as the named constant kReturnAddressBytes with a static_assert. The general form of the trap: any harness that derives an absolute stack address from a post-call sample is one word off, and a delta-only test suite will not notice.

A second, milder harness lesson is recorded in the code: two separate calls from the same C++ function do not necessarily start from the same absolute stack pointer (g++ -O0 gave two different ones), so a check that compared them directly failed at -O0 and passed at -O1 and above. It was replaced by a comparison of the two runs' DELTAS, which is the property the listing actually fixes and which is stable at every optimisation level.
